'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[Kursk offensive (2024–present)|Kursk offensive]]
***The [[Army of Ukraine|Ukrainian Army]] launches a new offensive in [[Kursk Oblast]], [[Russia]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c86wz0vd1dwo (BBC News)]
*[[Boko Haram insurgency]]
**Six [[Nigerian Armed Forces|soldiers]] and 34 [[Boko Haram]] gunmen are killed during a [[shootout]] in [[Borno State]], [[Nigeria]]. [https://apnews.com/article/nigeria-borno-extremists-boko-haram-clash-237e12f721343e21253a4ce60fd78201 (AP)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*[[82nd Golden Globe Awards]]
**The film ''[[Emilia Pérez]]'' and the television series ''[[Shōgun (2024 TV series)|Shōgun]]'' win the most awards at the 82nd [[Golden Globe Award|Golden Globes]] with four each. ''[[The Brutalist]]'' wins the awards for [[Golden Globe Award for Best Motion Picture – Drama|Best Motion Picture – Drama]], [[Golden Globe Award for Best Director|Best Director]] ([[Brady Corbet]]) and [[Golden Globe Award for Best Actor in a Motion Picture – Drama|Best Actor in a Motion Picture – Drama]] for [[Adrien Brody]]. [https://www.nbcnews.com/pop-culture/pop-culture-news/golden-globes-2025-winners-complete-list-rcna186300 (NBC News)]
**[[Fernanda Torres]] becomes the first [[Brazilians|Brazilian]] actress to win the award for [[Golden Globe Award for Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Drama|Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Drama]] for her performance in ''[[I'm Still Here (2024 film)|I'm Still Here]]''. [https://variety.com/2025/film/news/fernanda-torres-golden-globes-best-actress-drama-film-1236262309/ (Variety)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[January 2025 North American storm complex]]
**The [[National Weather Service]] issues [[Winter storm warning|winter storm alerts]] for areas covering nearly 70 million people from the [[Great Plains]] to the [[East Coast of the United States|East Coast]] of the [[United States]], with nearly 4 million currently under [[blizzard warning]]s. [https://www.cnn.com/2025/01/05/weather/winter-storm-weather-weekend/index.html (CNN)]
*A [[HAL Dhruv]] helicopter of the [[Indian Coast Guard]] crashes during a training flight in [[Porbandar]], [[Gujarat]], [[India]], killing all the three crew members. [https://web.archive.org/web/20250105105021/https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/coast-guard-helicopter-crashes-in-gujarat-during-training-sortie-report-101736063511488.html (The Hindustan Times)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Israel–United States relations]], [[United States support for Israel in the Israel-Hamas war]]
**The [[United States Department of State|U.S. State Department]] notifies [[United States Congress|Congress]] of a planned [[United States dollar|$]]8 billion arms sale to [[Israel]] consisting of [[air-to-air missile|air-to-air]] and [[AGM-114 Hellfire|Hellfire]] [[missile]]s, [[Shell (projectile)|artillery shells]], and other [[ammunition]]s. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cpvne94v1rdo (BBC News)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Capital punishment in the Democratic Republic of the Congo]]
**The [[Government of the Democratic Republic of the Congo|Congolese government]] [[Capital punishment|executes]] 102 individuals convicted of armed robbery and [[Banditry|urban banditry]], with an additional 70 prisoners reportedly awaiting execution. [https://apnews.com/article/congo-executes-kulunas-bandits-dc460aa0fc69489f2c1005b33796e0c9 (AP)]
*Former [[Vice President of Ecuador|Ecuadorian Vice President]] [[Jorge Glas]] is evacuated from [[Litoral Penitentiary|La Roca Prison]] in [[Guayaquil]] following an alleged [[assassination attempt]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/ecuadors-ex-vp-glas-evacuated-prison-after-attempted-killing-lawyer-says-2025-01-05/ (Reuters)]
*Resurfaced videos show [[Syria]]n [[Ministry of Justice (Syria)|Justice Minister]] [[Shadi al-Waisi]] overseeing the execution of two women in 2015 on [[prostitution]] charges according to [[Sharia]]. [https://www.newarab.com/news/syrian-minister-oversaw-execution-women-prostitution (The New Arab)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2024 Austrian legislative election#Government formation|2024–2025 Austrian government formation]]
**The ruling [[Austrian People's Party]] appoints [[Christian Stocker]] as its acting chairman to succeed [[Karl Nehammer]], who resigned as party leader and [[Federal Chancellor of Austria|Chancellor of Austria]] yesterday. Stocker says that he is open to negotiate with the [[Freedom Party of Austria]] to form the new [[2024 Austrian legislative election|post-election]] coalition government. [https://dnyuz.com/2025/01/05/new-austrian-conservative-leader-ready-for-coalition-talks-with-far-right/ (DNYUZ)]
*The [[Cabinet of Germany|German government]] reduces funding for two [[Israel|Israeli]] [[Human rights group|human rights groups]], [[Zochrot]] and [[New Profile]], that had advocated for [[Pro-Palestine|Palestinian rights]] and [[antimilitarism]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/germany-defunds-2-israeli-human-rights-groups/a-71217628 (DW)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2025 United Cup]]
**In [[tennis]], the [[United States at the United Cup|United States]] wins its second [[United Cup]] title after defeating [[Sport in Poland|Poland]] 2–0 in the final at the [[Ken Rosewall Arena]] in [[Sydney]], [[Australia]]. [https://www.reuters.com/sports/tennis/united-states-claim-second-united-cup-title-with-win-over-poland-2025-01-05/ (Reuters)]
